reason: SKILL.md:22 still says line-matched entries 'are annotated automatically' and that the agent's job is 'ONLY the judgment cases'. annotate-pr.md:59-61 and annotate-commit.md:45-47 still say 'line-matched entries annotate silently'. In the code, lib/annotate.sh:380-383 writes fi_auto_form, which is (PR-auto:)/(commit-auto:), whenever hook_auto=yes, and :547-551 prints 'Suggested ... will NOT close on sync' along with a --pick confirm command. Severity is downgraded because the hook's own context text says plainly to confirm with --pick (post-bash-dispatch.sh:250-257 and :285-292). The failure also leans the safe way: the entry stays open, and sync lists it as awaiting confirmation (sync.sh:396-406). It does not false-close. The Format section at SKILL.md:44 also leaves out the -auto and (verified:) tokens.
fix: Rewrite SKILL.md:22 and the 'When to invoke' paragraphs of annotate-pr.md and annotate-commit.md to say that hook output is a non-closing (PR-auto:)/(commit-auto:) suggestion, and that the agent must run the printed --pick for the entries the change really fixes. Add the -auto and (verified:) tokens to SKILL.md:44. Keep it within the 3700-byte budget in tests/docs-consistency.bats:102.

reason: In lib/annotate.sh:493-503 the line-overlap check (fi_line_matched) and the scope-limited check both run only when hook_auto=yes. Without the flag, any candidate that is the only citer of a touched file goes into auto_set, and :534 writes write_annotation, which stays canonical because of :380 (the closing (PR:)/(commit:) token). Since sync closes on canonical tokens with no further check, the manual path is weaker than the hook path. That contradicts the CHANGELOG 2.6.0 rationale ('touched is not fixed'). Three places steer agents onto this bare path: session-start.sh:464-467, SKILL.md:22 ('Run /found-issues:annotate-pr <N> manually'), and the legacy hook-off prompt at post-bash-dispatch.sh:216-221. An unrelated entry that is the only citer of any file the PR touches gets false-closed on merge, and nothing can reopen it.
fix: In fi_annotate_auto, write fi_auto_form unless annotate_all=yes (so with no flag it only suggests). Picks keep writing the canonical token. Change the session-start.sh:464-467 text to 'run `annotate-pr <N> --pick <path:line>` for the entries it fixes'. Update annotate-pr.md and annotate-commit.md (steps 4 and 'Possible outputs') and the matching tests.

reason: The guard in lib/annotate-commands.sh:234-245 runs before the --pick branch (:259), so `annotate-commit <merged-sha> --pick` exits 2 from any branch other than the default. fix.md:38-40 gives that command without mentioning --force. Severity is downgraded for three reasons. Phase 2 runs before Phase 3 creates the branch, so the run is often on the default branch, where the guard does not fire. The CLI's own error (:242) names --force for retroactive annotation. And a --force'd commit annotation that closes on the next sync carries about the same false-close risk as the sanctioned `resolve --verified ai` route.
fix: In fix.md bucket 1: for an identified already-merged fix, run `annotate-commit <sha> --force --pick <path:line>` only after `git show <sha> -- <path>` shows the symptom removed, and cite that evidence in the PR body. Otherwise use `found-issues resolve '<fragment>' --verified ai`.

reason: sync.sh:128 and :141 collect both commit-auto and PR-auto suggestions, but :403-405 prints a single confirm line for both, `annotate-commit <sha> --pick`. For a PR-auto entry that is the wrong command, and no sha is shown (:141 prints only the PR ref). For a landed commit-auto, running it from a non-default branch hits the ancestor guard at annotate-commands.sh:238-244 (exit 2). The only 'reject' route offered is 'delete the token by hand', which contradicts SKILL.md:48 hard rule 1. sync.md:32 documents only the one-line summary. This partly shares a root cause with prompt-3: the already-merged guard has no sanctioned confirm path.
fix: Print a confirm command per kind: `annotate-pr <N> --pick '<loc>'` for PR-auto, and `annotate-commit <sha> --force --pick '<loc>'` for a landed commit-auto, with the actual N/sha and loc filled in. Add a CLI reject verb (for example `annotate-reject <loc> <ref>` that strips the -auto token under the same tmp+mv path). Document the block in sync.md.

reason: defer.md:29 says false positives 'should be removed from the file entirely', but SKILL.md:48-49 (hard rules 1-2) forbids both direct writes and deleting [open] entries. defer.sh:133 and resolve.sh:131 tell the agent to 'manually remove the (PR: ...) annotation', and no CLI verb strips annotations. Severity is downgraded because sync already demotes CLOSED PRs to (PR-closed:) automatically. That leaves only an abandoned PR that is still open. A false positive can still be parked through `defer --reason`, so the agent is never fully stuck.
fix: Reword defer.md:29 to 'defer with --reason "not a real issue: ..."' (or add a dismiss verb). Add a narrow `unannotate <match> <ref>` subcommand and point the defer.sh:133 and resolve.sh:131 messages at it.

reason: pre-branch-delete.sh:356 prints the bypass ('set FOUND_ISSUES_PROMOTE_GUARD=off') in the stderr the agent reads. :76 honors that exact inline prefix, so the cheapest way for an agent to get unblocked is to bypass the guard. That contradicts SKILL.md:51 hard rule 4. The 'imprecise' half is weak. 'Run /found-issues:promote on the branch first' is accurate, because promote.sh:109-117 requires being on that branch. It is still not a concrete command sequence.
fix: Remove line :356 from the agent-visible message and leave it documented in docs/configuration.md. Replace :352-354 with the concrete sequence: `git checkout <branch> && found-issues promote`, then on a fresh branch off the default `found-issues promote --apply --from <branch>`, then PR, merge, delete.

reason: promote.sh:157 (listing) and :69 (apply) compare with verbatim `grep -Fxq`. pre-branch-delete.sh:299-307 and :322 compare dedup keys across open, deferred and fixed entries plus the archive. When main holds the entry as [fixed], [open] with an annotation, or archived, promote lists it as needing promotion, and --apply appends a fresh `- [open]` duplicate of a closed issue. Promote and the guard disagree on what 'promoted' means.
fix: Have both the promote listing and fi_promote_apply build main's keyset with fi_dedup_key_for_line over the main ledger plus the archive across all statuses, the same as pre-branch-delete.sh:299-307, and skip branch lines whose key is in that set. Better still, extract the keyset builder into a shared lib function.

reason: The code divergence is real. list-status.sh:58 and :99 resolve `${cwd:-${CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR:-$PWD}}`. annotate-commands.sh:123 and :249 call fi_find_issues_file with no argument, which defaults to $PWD (parse-entries.sh:23). fix.md:16 runs `list --json` without --cwd. fix.md:62-63 has no worktree, fetch or clean-tree step, and the per-day branch name collides on a second run the same day (`checkout -b` fails). Severity is downgraded from high because a mismatch makes --pick exit 1 ('no [open] entry matches', annotate.sh:192-193) rather than close anything. Whether the two ledgers actually diverge depends on whether Claude Code exports CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR into the Bash tool environment after EnterWorktree.
fix: Have fix.md pass `--cwd "$PWD"` to every list and status call. Add a Phase 0: a dedicated worktree, `git fetch`, branch from origin/<default> with a time or counter suffix, and refuse a dirty tree. Alternatively, make annotate-* resolve the same search root as list/status, or the reverse, so they agree in one place.
repro: In a Claude Code session, EnterWorktree into a worktree whose ledger differs from the main checkout, then run in the Bash tool: `echo "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR"; pwd; found-issues list --json | jq length; found-issues annotate-pr <N> --pick <loc-only-in-worktree>`.

reason: fix.md:82-88 has the agent run `annotate-pr <N> --pick` after `gh pr create`, which rewrites the tracked ledger in the working tree only (annotate.sh:173 mv). No step commits or pushes it, so the annotation lives only in that checkout. It is lost when the worktree is reaped, and it is absent from the checkout where SessionStart's autosync runs. The fix.md:18-20 resume rule also relies on that annotation persisting. fix.md:40-42 calls for an explicit `/found-issues:sync`, which auto-archives unless FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off (sync.sh:426-434) and leaves diffs in two tracked files with nothing committing them. The failure leans the safe way (entries stay open), so this is medium.
fix: Phase 4: after annotate-pr, `git add docs/found-issues.md` (only that path), commit, and push to the PR branch before merge. Run the closing sync as `FOUND_ISSUES_AUTO_ARCHIVE=off found-issues sync`, and either put any ledger diff in the PR or report it.

reason: fix.md:5 pre-authorizes only Bash(bats:*) as a test runner, while fix.md:67 and :79 require 'the repo's tests + build'. In a headless run without bypass permissions, npm, pytest or make calls get denied or prompt. The range-pick mismatch is real too. annotate.sh:43-45 renders `path:23-49`, and :124 matches by exact equality, so a pick built from `list --json` line=23 exits 1 with a visible 'no [open] entry matches' (annotate.sh:192-193). It fails loudly, never silently.
fix: Document that the dispatcher must pre-authorize the repo's test and build commands (or drop the bats-only implication). Tell the agent to build picks from `raw` as `path:line` or `path:line-line_end`, exactly as the candidate list prints them.

reason: session-start.sh:96-113 (the 'Prepend this single italicized line' directive plus `touch $ONBOARD_MARKER`) and :127-192 (the daily statusline nudge) are gated only on harness=claude, never on CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT. stop-reminder.sh:42-44, by contrast, skips non-cli entrypoints. A headless `claude -p` run therefore gets a directive that conflicts with fix.md:94-95's first-line scoreboard, and it uses up the once-ever onboarding hint where nobody will read it.
fix: Wrap both blocks in `if [[ -z "${CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT:-}" || "$CLAUDE_CODE_ENTRYPOINT" == cli ]]` so the marker is touched only in interactive sessions.

reason: SKILL.md:34-35 requires the marker on 'every substantive turn', but stop-reminder.sh:78-103 blocks only once per session (2.8.0), and only on mutating turns (:193-198). The 'full' message (:246-256) is chosen only when ~/.claude/found-issues/.onboarded is absent (:235-241), and session-start.sh:111 touches that file in the very first SessionStart, before any Stop. So the terse form (:244) is what effectively always fires. The terse form does list the three options, so it is usable, but it has no literal string to copy. That matters more if the rules never load at all (see prompt-17).
fix: Reword SKILL.md:34 to 'on the first substantive (editing or mutating) turn of a session'. Change the terse message to include the literal `<!-- found-issues-checked: none-noticed|logged|deferred -->` and one clause on what each option means.

reason: session-start.sh:65 strips only the frontmatter, so the 'Stop-hook marker (if enabled)' section (SKILL.md:32-35) reaches Codex. Codex never runs the Stop discipline: stop-reminder.sh:49-51 fails open, and install-codex-hooks registers no Stop hook. Running fi_codex_rewrite_core (lib/codex-rewrite.sh:18-23) leaves Claude tool names in place: codex-skills/fi-fix/SKILL.md:23 'Agent tool', fi-sync/SKILL.md:48 'Read tool', and fi-setup:56 and :187 'AskUserQuestion'. It also turns $ARGUMENTS into a bare `<the user-provided arguments>` inside bash fences (fi-log:16, fi-annotate-pr:14). One more instance: fi-setup:75 and :298 rewrite the literal `$ARGUMENTS` that the setup skill checks for in the Claude /fi alias file, which corrupts that check text.
fix: For harness=codex, cut the 'Stop-hook marker' section (an awk range from '## Stop-hook marker' up to the next '## '). Make tool references in commands/*.md harness-neutral. Have the rewrite emit `'<arguments>'` (quoted), and exempt the fi.md alias literal in setup.md from the $ARGUMENTS substitution.

reason: The --critical half is proven by the code. log.sh:26 honors --critical only as $1, and :38 joins the rest. For `src/a.sh:1 --critical — sym`, the location `src/a.sh:1 --critical` fails both line-spec regexes (they forbid whitespace) and falls into the `*/*` path branch, so it is logged with a spaced pseudo-path and no [!], and no error. The shell-splice half depends on the model. log.md:17 gives a bare `found-issues log $ARGUMENTS`, and its own example at :48 contains parentheses, which are a bash syntax error if spliced literally, but whether the model quotes them is runtime behaviour.
fix: Change log.md to `found-issues log [--critical] '<location — symptom (suggested: fix)>'` (single-quoted, with apostrophes escaped) and update SKILL.md:14 to match. In cmd_log, return 2 when ' --critical' appears anywhere other than $1.

reason: sync.md:4 declares '(no arguments)' and :16-18 runs a bare `found-issues sync`. sync.md:32 documents only `Synced. Closed: ...`. The CLI also prints 'Dry run — nothing written.', Demoted/Renamed counts, 'Synced. Nothing to close.', the status line, the awaiting-confirmation block (sync.sh:396-406) and an archive block (:431-434). It mitigates the flag risk, but only partly: when a command body lacks $ARGUMENTS, Claude Code appends the arguments to the prompt, so the model does see --dry-run, but forwarding it is up to the model. The CLI now rejects unknown flags (sync.sh:43-56).
fix: Change sync.md to `found-issues sync $ARGUMENTS` with argument-hint `[--dry-run]`. Replace :32 with a short list of the output sections and the action each one calls for (especially the awaiting-confirmation block; see prompt-4).

reason: SKILL.md:26 gives the literal `[fixed] (verified: ai) (fixed: <today>)` as the result to produce and never names `found-issues resolve` (lib/resolve.sh:15-34), the serialized path that sync.md:56-58 uses. SKILL.md:48 forbids direct writes in the same file. log.md:30 still refers to `@found-issues-rules.md`, which AGENTS.md says must not be used as an import. The Codex rewrite papers over this only for Codex (codex-rewrite.sh:22).
fix: Change SKILL.md:26 to 'close fixed ones with `found-issues resolve "<fragment>" --verified ai` — never by editing'. Change log.md:30 to 'per the found-issues rules'.

reason: What the repo says about how the rules reach Claude. It asserts but never proves: docs/architecture.md:88-89 ('loaded ... every session via the plugin spec auto-load mechanism (disable-model-invocation: true)'), :132-134, AGENTS.md:38, README.md:100, and CHANGELOG 0.1.0 at :1554. CHANGELOG :1624 explicitly lists 'Skill auto-loading behavior in a real session' as untested in CI, and no later entry closes that. tests/session-start.bats:405-408 actively pins that SessionStart does NOT inject the rules on Claude, and session-start.sh:37-39 delegates to the skill. hooks.json and plugin.json have no other injection path. No test exercises the skill-load path. By documented Claude Code semantics, disable-model-invocation:true makes a skill user-invocable only and removes it from the model's skill list, which is the opposite of preloading. Consistent with that, this session's skill list shows found-issues:fix, :log and :sync but no found-issues:rules, and no rules text is in context. On Claude, then, the rules probably reach the model only if the user types /found-issues:rules. The operator's global CLAUDE.md carries its own found-issues logging rule, which would hide this gap when the operator tests the plugin on his own machine.
fix: Have session-start.sh emit the rules body for harness=claude as well. That means lifting the :58 codex-only gate for the body (not the slash rewrite) and flipping tests/session-start.bats:405. Keep the skill as a user-invocable reference, or delete it so the content isn't duplicated. Correct architecture.md, AGENTS.md and README.md to describe the real mechanism.
repro: With the plugin installed, in a repo with no open ledger entries, run `claude -p 'If text headed "found-issues — agent rules" is in your context, quote its Hard rules section verbatim; otherwise reply NONE'`. Also run /context in an interactive session to see whether found-issues:rules is loaded.

reason: session-start.sh:397-415 picks the criticals plus the newest max_inject non-criticals, with no filter on (PR:)/(commit:) tokens. In-flight entries can crowd actionable ones out of the 15-entry cap. The :462-467 paragraph repeats the annotation guidance, and as prompt-2 shows, it points at the unsafe bare command. The cost is a few KB per session and only when there are more than 15 open entries. Showing in-flight entries also has some value, since it keeps the agent from re-logging them.
fix: Fill the slots with unannotated entries first, put annotated in-flight ones last, and count any overflow in the 'and N more' line. Fix the :464-467 text as described under prompt-2.

reason: status.md:16-17 says empty output means there are no open entries. lib/list-status.sh:221-228 prints `0 open` for an existing clean ledger and prints nothing only when no ledger file is found. The agent therefore misreports a missing ledger (or a wrong cwd) as a clean repo, and status.md never mentions the `0 open` form.
fix: Document `0 open` as the output for a clean ledger. Say that empty output means no ledger was found from this cwd (start one with /found-issues:log, or check the directory).
